newsitem.title: UK: More British men buying moisturiser, says report.
newsitem.headline: More British men buying moisturiser, says report.

text.p: British men are spending more money than ever before on toiletries, fuelled by changing attitudes to image and crafty marketing by manufacturers, according to a report published on Wednesday by Euromonitor, the market research group.

The British market for men's toiletries this year is expected to reach about 753 million pounds ($1.2 billion), Euromonitor said. By 2001, sales of men's toiletries are expected to rise 17 percent to 831.8 million, it said.

Manufacturers are using shaving regimes to launch new products such as fragrances and moisturisers. Young men are more willing to experiment with new products, because they see bodycare and fitness as indicators of a man's abilities and competence, the report said.

The reserve of older British men is being broken down by manufacturers who use technical or down-to-earth language in the packaging of toiletries to tempt potential customers without compromising their traditional images of masculinity, the survey found.

One of the key growth areas is bodycare, worth 100.3 million pounds in 1992 and 157.6 million pounds in 1996, Euromonitor said. But although more men are using deodorants and bodysprays, the most popular brands are established names such as Old Spice and Brut.
